heroHeading: Dubai & UAE: Where Desert Meets Opulence
heroSubheading: The UAE receives more five-star hotel rooms per capita than any nation on earth — yet the most extraordinary experiences here remain invisible to ordinary visitors. Behind the iconic skyline lies a world of private beach palaces, silent desert camps under the Milky Way, and yacht berths where the city's most powerful gather. Private Travel Club opens that world to you: no membership fees, no waiting lists, no compromises. Just the UAE as it was always meant to be experienced — entirely on your terms.

experiencesHeading: What to See and Do in Dubai & UAE

experiences.title: Private Desert Camp in the Liwa Mega Dunes
experiences.body: The Liwa Oasis sits on the edge of the Rub' al Khali — the largest continuous sand desert on earth. We arrange exclusive tented camps among dunes that rise to 300 metres, furnished with handwoven rugs, candlelit dining tables, and chilled Champagne waiting in the silence. Mornings begin with a private falconer demonstrating the UAE's oldest hunting tradition before a 4WD convoy takes you deeper into the Empty Quarter than any tour operator ventures. When night falls and the staff retreat, the desert belongs entirely to you and the constellations above.
experiences.imageAlt: Luxury desert camp in the UAE Liwa dunes at sunset

experiences.title: Superyacht Charter on the Arabian Gulf
experiences.body: The Arabian Gulf offers flat, warm waters, year-round sunshine, and a coastline studded with private islands and secluded anchorages that remain unknown to most visitors. We curate fully crewed superyacht charters departing from Dubai Marina or Abu Dhabi's Yas Marina — vessels ranging from 30-metre day boats to 60-metre expedition yachts with helipads. Itineraries can include a private anchorage off Sir Bani Yas Island, water-sports at the Musandam fjords, or a sunset passage beneath the sail-shaped silhouette of the Burj Al Arab, cocktails in hand as the city turns to gold.
experiences.imageAlt: Superyacht charter on the Arabian Gulf near Dubai

experiences.title: Exclusive Access to the Dubai Art & Design Scene
experiences.body: Design District d3 and Alserkal Avenue have quietly positioned Dubai among the world's most serious contemporary art markets. We arrange after-hours private viewings of gallery exhibitions, collector-hosted studio tours, and introductions to the curators who shape the region's cultural conversation. During Art Dubai or Design Days, we secure VIP preview access and arrange private dinners with artists and collectors in venues that never appear in any public programme. For clients building or refining a collection, we can facilitate introductions to the UAE's most respected private art advisors — discreetly, without commission conflict.
experiences.imageAlt: Dubai luxury architecture and design experience

experiences.title: Private Island Retreat at The World Archipelago
experiences.body: The World Islands — 300 private islands arranged in the shape of a world map off the Dubai coast — represent one of the most ambitious real estate projects ever constructed. Several islands are now privately held, and through our network we can arrange exclusive access to island estates not available through any public channel: private helicopter transfers from the mainland, dedicated staff, and the singular experience of watching the Dubai skyline glitter on the horizon from your own island terrace. For those wishing to explore acquisition, we can connect you with the relevant parties, entirely off-market.
experiences.imageAlt: Private island villa pool with Dubai skyline view

experiences.title: Helicopter Grand Tour of the Emirates
experiences.body: From the air, the UAE reveals itself as something almost surreal: the Palm Jumeirah's fronds spreading into the Gulf, the Hajar Mountains cutting across the Omani border, and the ancient fort towns of Al Ain rising from oasis palms. We arrange private helicopter itineraries that cover in a single day what would take a week by road — lifting from a hotel helipad in Dubai, crossing to the dramatic fjords of Musandam, touching down at a private falcon reserve in Ras Al Khaimah, and returning in time for dinner at height in the Burj Khalifa. Every routing is custom-built around your interests.
experiences.imageAlt: Private helicopter aerial view of the UAE Emirates

regions.name: Dubai: Marina, DIFC & Palm Jumeirah
regions.body: The three districts that define luxury Dubai each offer a distinct register. The Marina provides seafront living at its most animated — superyachts, waterside restaurants, and the most densely concentrated luxury residential towers on earth. DIFC is the financial and fine-dining nerve centre, where private members' clubs and Michelin-calibre restaurants sit above trading floors. The Palm Jumeirah is where privacy commands a premium: beachfront palace villas, ultra-luxury resorts, and the Atlantis The Royal — currently the most talked-about hotel address in the world.
regions.imageAlt: Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah luxury travel aerial view

regions.name: Abu Dhabi: Yas Island & Saadiyat
regions.body: Forty minutes from Dubai, Abu Dhabi operates at a quieter frequency — the capital's wealth is older, its public profile more reserved. Yas Island combines the world-class Yas Marina Circuit with private beach resorts and the extraordinary Louvre Abu Dhabi. Saadiyat Island is the cultural heart: the Louvre, the incoming Guggenheim, and Zayed National Museum are flanked by pristine beaches accessible only to resort guests. For clients seeking the Emirates without the spectacle, Abu Dhabi offers understated luxury at its most considered.
regions.imageAlt: Abu Dhabi Saadiyat Island luxury resort beach UAE

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah & The Northern Emirates
regions.body: An hour north of Dubai, the Hajar Mountains descend dramatically to the Gulf — a landscape that bears almost no resemblance to the flat desert most associate with the UAE. Ras Al Khaimah hosts the region's finest mountain retreat hotels, zip-line experiences above Jebel Jais (the UAE's highest peak), and a coastline still largely free of development. The ancient fort city of Al Ain, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, adds historical depth rarely found elsewhere in the Gulf. For those who want wilderness, silence, and altitude alongside their luxury, this is where the UAE reveals its other face.

faqsHeading: Frequently Asked Questions about Dubai & UAE Luxury Travel

faqs.question: How much does a private villa in Dubai cost per week?
faqs.answer: Private villa rentals in Dubai range considerably by location and specification. A fully staffed Palm Jumeirah beachfront villa typically starts from USD 15,000–25,000 per week; ultra-premium properties with private pools, boat docks, and dedicated concierge service can reach USD 80,000 or more. We source off-market residences not available through public rental platforms and ensure pricing is transparent with no hidden fees.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Dubai for luxury travel?
faqs.answer: The optimal window is November through April, when daytime temperatures sit between 22°C and 30°C — ideal for outdoor dining, beach days, yacht charters, and desert excursions. December and January coincide with Art Dubai season and the Dubai World Cup horse racing calendar, making these months particularly desirable. July and August are extremely hot but offer significant off-peak value on ultra-luxury properties and hotel suites.

faqs.question: Can I rent a private island near Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. The World Islands archipelago off the Dubai coast includes privately held islands available for exclusive rental through discreet channels. Access is typically via private helicopter or boat transfer from the mainland. Availability is limited and demand among serious enquirers is high — we recommend contacting us as early as possible, ideally three to six months before your preferred dates, to secure the best options.

faqs.question: Is a private jet into Dubai easy to arrange on short notice?
faqs.answer: Dubai International (DXB) and Al Maktoum International (DWC) are among the most private-aviation-friendly airports in the world, with dedicated FBO terminals, rapid customs processing, and excellent ground handling infrastructure. We can typically arrange a private jet departure or arrival with 24 to 48 hours' notice, depending on aircraft type and routing. For ultra-short-notice requests, we always explore every option before advising on feasibility.

faqs.question: What exclusive experiences in Dubai are not available to the general public?
faqs.answer: Our clients access desert camps in restricted areas of the Liwa Oasis, private island estates off The World archipelago, after-hours viewings at major galleries during Art Dubai, race-day hospitality suites at the Dubai World Cup, and introductions to falconry experts and private collectors. These experiences share one characteristic: they are not bookable online and require trusted local relationships built over years — which is precisely what Private Travel Club provides.

faqs.question: Do I need a membership to use Private Travel Club's services in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No membership fee is required, ever. Private Travel Club operates on a straightforward basis: you pay for the services and experiences we arrange on your behalf, with full transparency on costs before anything is confirmed. There are no joining fees, annual subscriptions, or retainers. Our 24/7 concierge team is available from the moment you make first contact — whether that is for a single trip or an ongoing travel partnership.
